messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] user defined link-function
parts:
Thanks for the quick reply,
I'm in the early stage of some study on mortality data using INLA. I'm using the binomial model with logit-link where:

y_t ~ Binomial(n_t, p_t)
p_t = exp(eta_t)/(1+eta_t)
eta_t = beta_0 + f(x1_t) + f(x2_t)
(like specified in some of your case studies)

I would instead like implement a binomial model where

p_xk = g_x/[(1-g_x^(1/c))e^t_k + g_x^(1/c)]^c
(x=age, k=year, g_x=mortality model, t_k=state vector, c=positive parameter, image shows the model)

Is this possible in INLA?

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] user defined link-function
parts:
yes,
g_x is a gomperz-makeham curve
g_x = 1-exp[-k0-k1*exp(k2*x)] where k0,k1,k2 are parameters and
t_k may be a gaussian random walk
